video_title: Draymond Green Reacts to Jason Kidd Getting Fired, Spurs & Knicks Upset Wins

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond discusses Jason Kidd's firing from the Mavericks and Masai Ujiri's influence.
quotes.excerpt: Jason Kidd just signed a four-year $40 million extension. So, again, leaving out the door with $40 million ain't that bad.
quotes.quote: Jason Kidd getting fired by the Mavericks. For starters, you have to number one, I didn't see this coming. Now, Masai Ujiri, getting the job as president of basketball and all the other things and you know, when Masai comes to a place, he gets total control. I was talking to a friend about this yesterday. Nobody is doing it like Masai Ujiri does it. Now, he comes in for him, of course, you're going to want your own coach, especially when you have the type of power that Masai Ujiri has when he goes to an organization. You're going to want your own coach, right? So he take a step back, he comes in. First thing he does, Jason Kidd out the door. Now Jason Kidd just signed a four-year $40 million extension. So, again, leaving out the door with $40 million ain't that bad. I do think Jason Kidd will get more head coaching opportunities. I actually think Jason Kidd did a very good job. So you assess this five-year tenure. You have I've seen a couple of miss playoffs because do mostly to injuries and then obviously this year, pretty sure the goal was to miss playoff. You have an NBA finals run. But more importantly, I think Jason Kidd came there to coach Luka Doncic and in the middle of Jason Kidd's run as the head coach of the Dallas Mavericks, Luka Doncic was traded away. So the team that he really came to coach, he got a chance to coach and actually has some success. Going to the NBA finals and obviously ultimately losing to the Boston Celtics. Also going to the Western Conference finals in 2022 and obviously losing to the Golden State Warriors. You take a step back and you look like it's pretty successful. And then obviously exceeded that losing this year because they were trying to lose. Pretty successful five-year tenure, I would say. And I would say this lines him up to if he wants to take one of these head coaching jobs coming up, the Trail Blazers, the Bulls, the Magic, I think he'll be in the race to get one of them. Because that's a really good tenure. Um, but the direction of the organization changed with the trading of Luka Doncic and then the firing of Nico Harrison, trading for AD and then trading out of AD, Kyrie Irving getting hurt, tearing his ACL, missing all of last year or this past year. The season that's still currently going. Like the whole direction changed over the course of his five years and yet and still, he still has some very successful years in there. So I don't expect to see Jason Kidd sitting very long now. In his contract, there may be an offset, meaning he go coach somewhere else, the $10 million a year that he's making, he probably don't get that. So, you could also expect Jason Kidd to not pick up one of these jobs and say, I'm going to wait at least two years, make these $10 million per year to do nothing and then I'll start to re-assess. Can't do that, wait for a better job. However, the one that sticks out the most to me on that list is the Portland Trail Blazers. Jason Kidd from Oakland. Damian Lillard return and also from Oakland. Point guard. Point guard, you look at Scoot Henderson and Young Guard. How can Jason Kidd help him? Right? So when you take a step back and you look at those jobs, I definitely can see Jason Kidd taking the Trail Blazers job. Now, however, it's been widely known that their coach, excuse me, that the owner of their team doesn't want to pay the head coach. It's it's been widely publicized. It's been, you know, a lot of people have been talking about it. And quite honestly, you're making $10 million to do nothing and this coach trying to pay a million to excuse me. Tom Dundon wants to pay a million or two million dollars. I think that will run Jason Kidd the opposite way. But when I look at the Trail Blazers roster, that looks like the team that Jason Kidd will feel most confident on this list and going into next year saying, yo, we got a chance to compete. The Orlando Magic also is a team that's going into next year you saying can compete. The Bulls not so much. So I wouldn't expect him to even interview for the Bulls job. But if he wants any of these jobs, he'll definitely be right at the top of the list because his five-year tenure with the Mavericks were extremely successful.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond praises Victor Wembanyama's Game 1 performance, comparing it to all-time playoff games.
quotes.excerpt: Was Wby's Game 1 a top five playoff performance you've ever seen? He had 41 points, 24 rebounds.
quotes.quote: Was Wby's Game 1 a top five playoff performance you've ever seen? He had 41 points, 24 rebounds, on 56% shooting, 49 minutes played, two blocks. It has to be up there for the top games because you have to put in context what's actually happening. And what I mean by that is, this team, this young fella, just went on the road versus the defending champions. The night Shai Gilgeous-Alexander was presenting his MVP award, without their starting point guard, and they went on the road. He did everything he had to do including hitting a bomb from no man's land. He did everything he had to do to make sure they won that game. Including defensively, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander struggled and a large part of that is, these guys aren't recovering. I've always said when Shai gets to going downhill, you can't recover and try to cut them off. You have to ride him and almost let him go. Well, them letting him go, he's running into Victor Wembanyama. So some of the shots that Shai normally takes, he didn't even take. Some of the shots he normally make, he took and short armed them. That's the presence of Victor Wembanyama. And so when you talk about top five playoff performances, this has to be up there. Another one that comes to mind is Klay Thompson Game 6 in OKC. Has to be up there. Down three to one, coming back from that to force a Game 7, that has to be up there. You think LeBron James Game 5 versus the Detroit Pistons? That one has to be up there. Right? You're talking the all-time top five playoff performances that I've seen. Right? That is three of them. Steph Curry Game 4. Steph Curry Game 4 in Boston. Has to be up there for top five playoff performances that I've seen. And the fifth top five playoff performance that I got to go with that I've seen and I I have to use this one because quite honestly it affected me. In getting the ring. Kawhi Leonard versus the Philadelphia 76ers to do all that he had to do to then game them boys in the corner with the double bounce shot. Neil over. I got to go with that one. That was an elite performance. Ultimately, you know, started the the road to Toronto Raptors first and only NBA championship. So I got to go with that one. That's my top five performances that I've ever seen, but Victor Wembanyama, he's definitely up there.

I said De'Aaron Fox has to play great. It almost has to be him over Wby. Look like he'd been here before. I mean, Dillon Harper, wow. Wow. Had no clue that he was this special. You know, and you've seen it building over the year. But man, Dillon Harper with his play, he takes this team from being in the pipeline to win a championship soon to like, the way he's playing, they can win a championship right now. I mean, he is unbelievable. Special. Knows how to use his size, knows when to use his speed. Getting more and more comfortable with the jump shot. People, he's not even super comfortable with his three ball yet. Imagine once next year, next two years he come and he just rising up from three two. Yo. And and it's pure basketball. It's pure like no foul baiting, no none of that just like, yo, I'm scoring, you can't stop me. Every time I got a smaller guard, I realized that I'm getting to the hole finishes around the basket extremely well. He's special. He is special. Stephen Castle, you already know how I feel about Stephen Castle, but he is special. Between these two guards and Victor Wembanyama, OKC, listen. The San Antonio Spurs are right now in the midst of building a dynasty. These two teams slash people will determine who actually does it and who doesn't. And right now, what's so important for the San Antonio Spurs are? You know this is this is a head, right? Like if the Thunder win this series, they they automatically in the build up of this rivalry, holds the advantage. And what I mean not the they won advantage. I mean the mental advantage. Because once they beat you once, now you come back next year or two years or three years from now, you're going to remember that. And they're going to remember that. And they're going to feel like they big they can big bro you. And then you got to overcome that, which is even tougher. And so this series right now is so important. So important for what the next five years or so, 10 years possibly looks like in the NBA. It is so important. Going to need a bit more from Chet Holmgren. Chet Holmgren's talked about this rivalry. Everybody's talked about this rivalry with Victor Wembanyama and then like Chet's not really guarding him. And I can understand that from a standpoint of Chet's coming over and whooping stuff. Similar to a game plan we'll talk about later. I can understand it if there's like this game plan adjustment that's like, yo, we want him here so he can do this. But it it almost came off to me is like he didn't want that smoke. And Wby want all that smoke. You know, most cases, you know, somebody asked you, oh man, you you were you motivated by that guy getting MVP trophy? Most cases people going to be like, oh no, not really. I don't know if it's the language barrier or or or Wby is just cut like that. But he come out and say, yeah. I was. Of course. Right? So I love the mindset. I love the demeanor. I love how he's approaching it. Or swag in front of their bench. The face of the NBA, everybody been arguing who is going to be. Wby said it's me. I'm that. And he's doing that. Alex Caruso had an incredible game for the Thunder, 31 points on 57% shooting. Unfortunately for Alex Caruso, his 31 points could never be what Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's 31 points are because it just does something different to the defense. Now, you take that from someone who's had 30 plus points in very meaningful games and it not being Steph Curry. It just does something different. It causes a different reaction. The amount of points that other guys are getting off of that star player because they're getting those points is also bigger, right? So that the impact is much larger. So Alex Caruso, incredible game off the bench 31. Unfortunately for OKC, if it's not Shai getting off, but Alex Caruso, it doesn't really guarantee you wins. And that's just an unfortunate, you know, side of the NBA. Yeah, you want to come out, you want to play great, but you need your stars to play great in order to win at a high level. Jaylen Williams said post game that Wby's presence affects his decision making. Listen, welcome to the world of all of us in the NBA. You have to always know where he is. And due to that, you can't play split second basketball. You can't make quick decisions. You always got to be lurking to know where he is, which can throw the time and off a lot of things. Right? But it was good to see J-Dub back out there. He had a great game. A lot of minutes. So it I thought at some point they pull them going into Game 2 on one day rest. Coming off a hamstring, those things can get tricky. You know, so that's I think that's something to watch for. Uh but you know, you have to ask yourself the question, what can OKC do from a game plan and rotation standpoint? And adjustments that they need to make. Well, number one, I think they're going to have to play Isaiah Joe more. They're going to need shooting. Pretty much what San Antonio is saying is we're packing the paint and you're going to have to beat us from the three-point line. Lu Dort, you're going to have to beat us from the three-point line. Right? There all of these guys, Chet Holmgren, you're going to have to beat us from the three-point line. Cason Wallace, who's been shooting incredibly. You're going to have to beat us from the three-point line. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, you're going to have to beat us from the three-point line. By the way, if you think you're not going to have to, we got this big fella down there. Go ahead and see how that looks for you. Right? So, they're doing what everyone has always believed OKC need what would need to be done to OKC for them to beat you on your terms, which is make them beat you from the three-point line. However, no one else has Victor Wembanyama at the rim. And so that that changes things a bit, right? But I think they got to get more shooting out there on the floor. Um I think Chet Holmgren is going to have to to take on the challenge. I think they're going to actually aside from having more shooting on the floor, they're going to need to deploy their two big lineup, I think, a bit more because for Victor Wembanyama, that size on the back side makes a difference, right? So if you say you got Chet Holmgren in the action, guarding Victor Wembanyama and you got Harden seen on the back side. That size on the back side makes a different a huge difference when you're playing against Victor Wembanyama. And so, listen, yes, OKC can do it. Uh but the Spurs, they were four and one against these guys for a reason. Uh they present some challenges that are tough for OKC. Yes, they can figure it out. They're going to need to make more shots. Um we'll see De'Aaron Fox coming back. Uh, you know, how does this affect Dillon Harper, right? Dillon Harper's been playing great. Even coming off the bench, I think he'll continue to play great. Um, but De'Aaron Fox coming back, what I spoke about in Game 1, De'Aaron Fox still got to have that same mentality. You must have elite level guard play in order to win at a high level in the NBA playoffs. And so De'Aaron Fox will need to play huge. You're going to need Stephen Castle to just do what he do, right? And then it always comes up huge. And then you're going to need a great game from Wby. Now, you got to go in if you're the OKC, if excuse me, if you're the San Antonio Spurs, you got to go into this game like, yo, this is our chance to go up 2-0 going back home. You got to come out nasty, thirsty, hungry, physical. And Wby got to be dominant. Will it be 49 and 24? Maybe not. But he got to be dominant and he got to dominate the way he's been doing.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond criticizes Cavaliers' tactical errors in guarding Josh Hart during Knicks' historic comeback.
quotes.excerpt: Jalen Brunson living on an island with James Harden guarding him. That's just not something you can let happen.
quotes.quote: And our other Game 1 in the Eastern Conference Finals, the Knicks come back to beat the Cavs 115 to 104 in overtime. Take a 1-0 series lead, which means the Cavs scored three points in overtime. This was 101 to 101 going into overtime. The Knicks rally from down 22 points in the fourth quarter. And if you're watching the game, you can see exactly what happened. Jalen Brunson finished with 38 points and six assists on 51% shooting. Landry Shamet and Michael Bridges hit some clutch threes in the fourth and overtime, which is what we need to talk about. So Jalen Brunson gets going in the fourth quarter and goes ballistic. Expected from Jalen Brunson. What wasn't expected was the way it happened. Expected in a sense, but I didn't think they'd quite let it happen. And that is Jalen Brunson living on an island with James Harden guarding him. That's just not something you can let happen. Like James Harden's been at it for 17 years. Teams have tried this over and over again. You have to expect that this is what they're ultimately going to go to. And so you have to have some other coverage, a show with James, in covers, right? Put James on the guy that you're not worried about making plays in the pocket. Do some other things right there. James, you're blitzing and then you're getting like, but this isn't just a coaching issue. Like, yeah, if you're Kenny Atkinson, you want to adjust sooner. But this isn't just on Kenny Atkinson. When you're trying to compete at a championship level, you must have guys that want to take on that challenge. I'm not switching at this point in the game. I'm getting through this screen the first one. And by the way, the problem I'll be having with most of these guys are, you set the screen they switch. Set the screen, let them set the first screen, don't switch. Let them set the second screen, don't switch. Fought through it. They don't just want to give the ball to the other guy. Jalen Brunson want to make the play. So don't switch the first one. Don't switch the second one. Now as opposed to Jalen Brunson getting the ball with uh getting the switch with 19 seconds on the shot clock, 17 seconds on the shot clock. Now he gets to switch with six or seven seconds on the shot clock. Now you got to go. Now our defense can react and we just end up in a rotation. But it's not just dicing us up, tearing us apart. And that's what happened last night. They just switched every time. But you must have guys that want to take on that challenge. And who would take on that challenge? Dennis Schroder would take on that challenge. Dennis Schroder was taking on that challenge. When Dennis Schroder left the game, things got a little bleak. Because you got guys in there that don't really want that challenge. They don't want to fight through the screen and say this my match up I want to stop this guy. They don't do it. I watched this every night in these big time playoff games. A guys who, man, I'm a defender. I want to defend and you switch every fucking time it's an opportunity to. Every time. And I don't understand it. I don't understand it. Guys simply don't know how to win, don't want to win, don't want to do what it takes for some of along those lines. But it's ridiculous. Watching these guys just switch off. Ain't James Harden to job to guard Jalen Brunson? It's not. No matter how you want to slice it. It is not James Harden's job to guard Jalen Brunson one-on-one. It's not. It's not what he's paid to do. Some of those other guys who just switching off, it is your fucking job. So everybody want to come out and say, oh man, James Harden got annihilated. They're picking on him. They should fucking pick on him. Why not? You tire them out. Absolutely pick on him. So all of a sudden them threes that will fall late, they fall short. Yeah, pick on him. It's the Cavs job responsibility not to allow it. But something tactical happened here. 2015. Tactical and technical. 2015, Steve Kerr Game 4, Golden State Warriors second round versus the Memphis Grizzlies making an adjustment that changes everything. Steve Kerr makes an adjustment to put Andrew Bogut on Tony Allen and not guard him. Draymond, you're on Marc Gasol, you're guarding him straight up, but Bogut will be around to help if you need it, but you got him straight up. Harrison Barnes, you are fronting Zach Randolph. You're not making contact with his body. Bogut, you're mirroring him everywhere he go. Not guarding Tony Allen. And I've watched the Cleveland Cavaliers deploy a similar strategy with Josh Hart. And Josh Hart was playing great in the first half. Double digit scoring, all of that. But a lot like I talked about Alex Caruso, it don't matter. Because what it was doing to everyone else offensively was an issue. The paint was clogged, there was nowhere to go. KAT couldn't get off. Jalen Brunson was doing, you know, getting to the floaters, but couldn't get all the way to the rim much. And then everything changed when Landry Shamet was out there and Josh Hart came out the game. Now if you're Mike Brown, you're going to have to figure out ultimately in this series how you can come back the way they are guarding Josh Hart. Because you need Josh Hart's intensity, you need what he brings to this team. He brings dog, he brings a lot to this so you need it. We did we deployed that strategy and when we deployed that strategy, it took Tony Allen off the floor. Once it took Tony Allen off the floor, they were no longer good enough to guard us on the offensive end. So, that was the series. They never won another game. This is what they're doing to Josh Hart. A similar, putting the big on them and they're not guarding. You want to hit the three, go ahead. You want to hit three of them, go ahead. We don't care. We want to keep Carl Anthony Towns and Jalen Brunson out. Carl Anthony Towns has been at the top of the floor making all the plays for this group throughout the playoffs. With with with Josh Hart out there, and the way they guard him, it put Carl Anthony Towns in the corner. And that's not going to ultimately be a recipe for success for the Knicks. But by the way, Knicks fans, don't be having a fucking parade yet. Let the Knicks win the series first. And then go after another one before y'all throw a parade. But got to tip my cap. It was a hell of a Game 1. And I'm looking forward to Game 2. Also looking forward to seeing how they're going to use Josh Hart and not allow the Cleveland Cavaliers to use Josh Hart against them. That's going to be the biggest adjustment. And then the Cleveland Cavaliers, the ball start everybody say the ball stopped. The ball stopped moving. Let me tell you when the ball stopped moving. The ball stopped moving when they when they started going the hacker of Mitchell Robinson. They start hacking Mitchell Robinson. The score, Mitchell Robinson was missing free throws. Cleveland wasn't gaining more separation, 14, 15, 17, 14. And in turn, they lost all their offensive flow because you're playing off a free throw every play against a set defense. That's when they lost all their offensive flow. Wasn't that the ball just stop moving. They deployed the hacker shack hacker Mitchell. And when they did that, lost all their offense to floor and they were never able to get it back. That's when the game changed. Ultimately, you out think smart yourself sometimes, it happens in this business. I think if Kenny could take that one back, he would because they were rolling and they were getting the stops that they needed. So, I don't think we'll see that one again. Change your offense, it change the game.
